doffing: And then, doffing one's own headpiece, how strange to assume for a moment some one's--any one's--to be a man of valour who has ruled the Empire; to refer while Brangaena sings to the fragments of Sophocles, or see in a flash, as the shepherd pipes his tune, bridges and aqueducts.
doff:
Where Faith rod-chastened smiles to rise
And doff its fears,
And carping Sorrow pines and dies--

Through my body, crying, “Strip!
Doff this new exuberance.
Come and dance the Lover’s Dance!”

Silver snakes that once a year
Doff the lovely coats you wear,
Seek no covert in your fear

To men no more than so much cover
For them to doff or try,
I found in Death a constant lover:
